summary.headline: GSP Crop Science Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19.5% to ₹258 crore, but EBITDA fell to ₹73.6 crore (margin 13.2%) on raw material costs.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew about 19.5% year on year to roughly ₹258 crore, driven mainly by higher realisations from price increases. EBITDA fell to ₹73.6 crore from ₹93.2 crore, with margin at 13.2%, as raw material costs, supply chain disruptions and a lower share of high-margin products weighed. H1 FY27 revenue rose about 12% to ₹944 crore, while H1 EBITDA margin was 12.3%. Management attributed part of the profit decline to a weak monsoon (about 87% of normal, El Niño) that slowed domestic demand in August and September. Management expects margins to recover in Q4 FY27 with the rabi season.

financial_highlights.change: vs ≈₹135 crore in H1 FY26 (figure garbled in transcript; ₹116 crore inferred from 12.3% margin on ₹944 crore)
H1 boosted by fixed asset sale gains and forex gains

segments.name: Domestic B2B
segments.commentary: Main driver of H1 revenue growth; growth was mostly realisation-led, with some volume gains in certain products.

segments.name: Exports (Latin America, South East Asia)
segments.commentary: Export growth of about 20% cited on the call, but management said growth came mainly from domestic markets. Exports are about 20% of total business, targeted at about 25% in three years.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 expected to be subdued on prices and realisations; Q4 FY27 expected to see better prices and realisations with the rabi season.
Gross margin expected to see further pressure next quarter, then return to normal levels by Q4 FY27.
Management expects sequential EBITDA margin improvement in Q3 and Q4.
Exports expected to rise to about 25% of revenue within three years.
Brazil business expected to become feasible in two to three years once enough registrations are in place (two registrations being acquired).
R&D spend at about 2.5% of revenue, planned to increase from next year.
capex_capacity: Backward integration of key technicals is a stated priority to reduce reliance on imports.
Brazil subsidiary set up about three years ago, with a small administration office for B2B business; platform expected to be ready in a year or two.
Investment in product registrations in Brazil ongoing.
Raw material imports are about 40-45% of total raw material requirement, mainly from China.
demand_pricing: Demand was subdued in domestic B2B and B2C from July onward as the dry August and September slowed sales; the market focused on liquidating inventory.
Raw material cost increases were the main driver of gross margin compression.
Power, fuel and manpower costs also rose.
Farmers are delaying spend and shifting some acreage to less water-intensive crops, and reluctant to spend on crop protection when early-stage rainfall is deficient.
Management said the south faces reservoir constraints affecting second paddy; chilli, grapes and pulses were less affected.
Brazil faces delayed customer buying, liquidity constraints, vessel availability and longer shipping times.

qa_highlights.question: How wide is the portfolio to address pollution and weather-related crop stress, and how is the company placed?
qa_highlights.answer: Presence in fruits, vegetables and some pulses; a recently launched patented insecticide is helping. Management expects better performance than last year in the rabi/kharif season despite micro-environment challenges.

qa_highlights.question: Will the weather-driven sowing delays normalise soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sowing delays are in some geographies and expects normalisation within about 30 days, though second paddy in the south may be a challenge due to reservoir levels.

qa_highlights.question: What drove revenue growth and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly domestic B2B and realisation-led, with some volume increases. Margins did not follow revenue growth because of raw material cost pressures.

qa_highlights.question: What was the margin pressure breakdown in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% from raw material costs, 20-30% from supply chain issues, and about 20% from lower sales of high-margin products. Gross margin fell from 40% to 34%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D spend and will it rise?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is about 2.5% of revenue and is planned to rise from next year, given backward integration and product plans.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normal level of other income?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹20 million per quarter normally; the H1 jump came from the sale of a fixed asset parcel.

risks_watch: Below-normal monsoon (about 87% of LPA) and El Niño, with expected below-normal rainfall in October to December, could hit rabi acreage and input demand.
Raw material price inflation and dependence on Chinese imports (40-45% of raw materials).
Brazil registrations and logistics (vessel availability, transit time) remain constraints; the timeline is two to three years.
Margin recovery depends on Q4 price and realisation improvement; Q3 expected to be subdued.
Power and fuel cost increases and manpower cost escalation.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on the near term: management repeatedly tied the margin squeeze and weak demand to raw material costs and the weak monsoon, while being confident that Q4 margins will recover. Answers were sometimes vague or repetitive on Brazil and export numbers, and the transcript is partly garbled.
key_quotes: So overall we are a very profited company and we have not been a bigger share of our business.
So we see that it will normalize in Q4.
Yes, the equity margin should improve sequentially in the coming quarter, considering the kind of products that we expect for Rabi and the Q4 being at the brief movement period that is there.

growth.why: Management guided only to a margin recovery to normal levels by Q4 FY27 and sequential EBITDA margin improvement in Q3 and Q4, with no numeric growth target; the stated support is rabi-season pricing and realisations, with no specific capacity, orders or contracts behind it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects sequential EBITDA margin improvement in Q3 and Q4 and gross margin back to normal by Q4, from Q2 EBITDA margin of 13.2% versus 12.3% H1 and gross margin down from 40% to 34%, though Q3 is guided subdued.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No plant or line expansion discussed; the only platform work is the Brazil administration office, expected ready in a year or two, with Brazil feasible in two to three years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue grew 19.5% but mainly on realisation; management guided Q3 subdued and volume recovery depends on rabi season, with sowing delays expected to normalise in about 30 days.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex amount or utilisation level was given; backward integration is only a stated priority with no timing.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is qualitative only and tone is cautious, with Q3 expected subdued and a weak monsoon at about 87% of normal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin recovery depends on Q4 price and realisation improvement after a subdued Q3, with raw material costs (40-45% imported from China) and El Niño-driven below-normal Oct-Dec rain as risks.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product launch was named; only a recently launched patented insecticide was mentioned, with no further timing.

rows.label: Brazil registrations and subsidiary build-out
rows.why: Two registrations being acquired; Brazil expected feasible in two to three years, but constrained by customer liquidity, vessel availability and longer shipping times.

rows.label: Exports rising to 25% of revenue
rows.why: Exports about 20% of business with about 20% export growth cited, but management said growth came mainly from domestic markets, so the 25% target is a stated goal rather than a committed plan.

rows.label: Backward integration of key technicals
rows.why: Stated priority to reduce reliance on imports, with 40-45% of raw materials imported mainly from China, but no capex amount or date was given.

tone.note: Management was confident that Q4 margins will recover with the rabi season and pricing, but cautious on Q3, the weak monsoon and raw material costs; analysts pressed on the margin breakdown and export and Brazil numbers, which were vague.
